```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(measure)
library(recipes)
library(measure.sec)
```

An integration window selects the part of a chromatogram used for molecular
weight calculations. Exclusion regions remove intervals within that support.
The same selection applies to molecular weight averages, fractions, and
distributions.

This example uses synthetic, uniformly concentrated material at constant flow.
The signal is proportional to mass concentration, and the supplied standards
define a decreasing log10 molecular-weight calibration in g/mol. The example
demonstrates numerical selection; it does not qualify an instrument or identify
which intervals should be excluded from a real sample.

## Build a complete recipe

```{r synthetic-input}
axis <- seq(0, 10, by = 0.1)
curve <- new_measure_tbl(axis, rep(1, length(axis)))
data <- tibble::tibble(sample_id = "sample")
data$ri <- new_measure_list(list(curve))
standards <- data.frame(location = c(0, 5, 10), log_mw = c(6, 5.5, 5))
```

The window keeps elution times 1 through 9. The integration exclusion removes
times 4 through 6, leaving two separate intervals. The helper below builds an
ordinary recipe so subsequent examples can change one selection explicitly.

```{r selected-recipe}
selected_recipe <- function(
  data,
  integration_range = NULL,
  regions = tibble::tibble(start = 4, end = 6)
) {
  recipe(~ ., data = data) |>
    update_role(sample_id, new_role = "id") |>
    step_sec_conventional_cal(
      measures = "ri",
      standards = standards,
      fit_type = "linear",
      extrapolation = "none"
    ) |>
    step_sec_integration_window(
      measures = "ri", start = 1, end = 9, auto_detect = FALSE
    ) |>
    step_sec_exclude_regions(
      measures = "ri", regions = regions, purpose = "integration"
    ) |>
    step_sec_mw_averages(
      measures = "ri", integration_range = integration_range
    ) |>
    step_sec_mw_fractions(
      measures = "ri", cutoffs = 10^5.5,
      integration_range = integration_range
    ) |>
    step_sec_mw_distribution(
      measures = "ri", type = "both", n_points = 60,
      integration_range = integration_range
    )
}

fit <- prep(selected_recipe(data))
result <- bake(fit, new_data = NULL)
result |>
  dplyr::select(sample_id, mw_mn, mw_mw, mw_dispersity, dplyr::starts_with("frac_"))
```

The calibration step records which MW curve belongs to `ri`; the three
consumers select that curve. Signal and calibration locations must align.
Selected boundaries between samples are interpolated: concentration linearly,
and MW in the declared scale of its curve. Calibration is never extrapolated
to fill missing positive-mass support. A boundary must coincide with a finite
MW sample or be bracketed by finite samples. When a nominal calibration domain
ends between samples and extrapolation is disabled, select finite sampled
support; the unsampled endpoint strips are omitted rather than assigned mass.

Each retained interval receives its own trapezoidal weights. No trapezoid
connects the two sides of an exclusion. Baseline-only exclusions do not remove
mass from these calculations; `purpose = "integration"` and `"both"` do.

## Read the selected distribution

The two retained intervals have equal mass. The cutoff is inside the excluded
gap, so the below-cutoff fraction and the CDF plateau are both one half.

```{r selected-mass}
density <- result$ri_differential[[1]]
cdf <- result$ri_cumulative[[1]]
below_column <- grep("^frac_below_", names(result), value = TRUE)
area <- sum(diff(density$location) *
  (head(density$value, -1) + tail(density$value, -1)) / 2)
gap <- cdf$location > 5.41 & cdf$location < 5.59

stopifnot(
  isTRUE(all.equal(result[[below_column]], 0.5, tolerance = 1e-8)),
  isTRUE(all.equal(area, 1, tolerance = 1e-8)),
  all(abs(cdf$value[gap] - 0.5) < 1e-8),
  !anyDuplicated(cdf$location)
)
cdf[gap, ]
```

```{r selected-density, fig.alt = "A normalized molecular-weight density with two retained intervals and zero density across the shaded excluded interval."}
ggplot2::ggplot(density, ggplot2::aes(location, value)) +
  ggplot2::annotate("rect", xmin = 5.4, xmax = 5.6,
    ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "#FF9933", alpha = 0.15) +
  ggplot2::geom_path(linewidth = 0.7, colour = "#4A90A4") +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "log10 molecular weight (g/mol)",
    y = "Mass fraction per log10(MW)"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()
```

At a discontinuity, the differential curve repeats a location to store its
one-sided values in row order. `geom_path()` preserves those vertical jumps.
The CDF has unique locations and is suitable for regular interpolation.
`n_points` specifies a target regular grid; support boundaries are added when
needed, so a selected distribution can contain additional rows.

When `mw_range` displays only part of the distribution, normalization still uses
the total selected mass. Cropping a plot does not renormalize its visible
portion to one. Fractions apply their cutoff to sampled MW values; resolution
near a cutoff still matters.

## Override a stored window

An explicit `integration_range` takes precedence over the row's stored window.
Integration-purpose exclusions always apply to the resulting range.

```{r explicit-range}
override <- bake(prep(selected_recipe(data, integration_range = c(0, 3))),
  new_data = NULL)
tibble::tibble(
  selection = c("Stored window minus exclusion", "Explicit range 0 to 3"),
  mw = c(result$mw_mw, override$mw_mw)
)
```

## Keep selection attached to the sample

`step_sec_exclude_regions()` can match regions by `sample_id`. Consumers read
each row's current metadata when baking, including after serialization and
reordering.

```{r sample-specific-regions}
samples <- tibble::tibble(sample_id = c("A", "B"))
samples$ri <- new_measure_list(list(curve, curve))
regions <- tibble::tibble(
  sample_id = c("A", "B"), start = c(4, 3), end = c(6, 4)
)
trained <- unserialize(serialize(prep(selected_recipe(samples, regions = regions)), NULL))
original <- bake(trained, new_data = NULL)
reordered <- bake(trained, new_data = samples[2:1, ])
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(original$mw_mw, rev(reordered$mw_mw))))
reordered |> dplyr::select(sample_id, mw_mw)
```

If the selection contains no retained support, moments and fractions are `NA`
and distribution curves are empty.

```{r empty-support}
empty <- bake(prep(selected_recipe(data, integration_range = c(4.5, 5.5))),
  new_data = NULL)
stopifnot(is.na(empty$mw_mw), nrow(empty$ri_differential[[1]]) == 0)
```
